newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks edge up to six-year high close.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks edge up to six-year high close.

text.p: Taiwan stocks edged up to another six-year high close on Friday on strong electronics buying, defying heavy profit-taking pressure in many industrials and Wall Street's overnight tumble, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 7.42 points or 0.09 percent higher at 8,275.57 after rising as high as 8,308.55 at the opening and falling as low as 8,221.46.
Friday's close surpassed the 8,268.15 finish of March 13 to marked the index's highest close since it reached 8,569.55 on May 15, 1990. Turnover was hectic T$146.66 billion.
Brokers said the market's strong early rise was buoyed mainly by news of a government proposal to privatise the Big Three state-run banks -- Chang Hwa Bank, First Bank, Hua Nan Bank.
A government panel has suggested the Provincial Assembly junk its 1989 decision not to let state stakes in the Big Three state-run banks fall below 51 percent, officials said.

The Big Three banks were hit by last-minute profit-taking that erased their early-session gains. Chang Hwa Bank and First Bank closed unchanged at T$186 and T$188, respectively, while Hua Nan Bank was down 50 cents or 0.34 percent to T$145.
"Some investors turned cautious on a sharp rise in the financial sector," said National Securities analyst Eric Liu.
Several brokers noted it was a common market perception that sharp rises in the heavily weighted financial sector were normally accompanied by declines in industrials.
Wall Street's overnight tumble and downturns in other Asian markets slightly dampened market sentiment, but brokers said investors' optimistic outlook remained largely unchanged.
Electronics, which encountered profit-taking in previous sessions, helped carry the market by rebounding 1.19 percent.
